title: Domestic abuse prevention orders a 'step in right direction'

input.lead: Domestic abuse charity Endeavour welcomed the national rollout but said more work was needed
input.summary: Domestic abuse charity Endeavour welcomed the national rollout but said more work was needed
input.evidence_text: Domestic abuse prevention orders a 'step in right direction' - BBC News Image caption, Jill Caldwell, who is chief executive of domestic abuse charity Endeavour, welcomed the new orders By Mairead Smyth , North West and Lauren Hirst , North West Published 1 hour ago A charity has welcomed the rollout of domestic abuse protection orders (DAPOs) across England and Wales but warned more needs to be done to protect and support victims. Under new restrictions, abusers could be forced to hand over house keys, social media passwords, phones and laptops in a bid to protect victims. Jill Caldwell, chief executive of Bolton-based domestic abuse charity Endeavour, said the rollout was "a really good start" but the government needed to ensure the orders were effectively enforced by police and specialist support services were in place for victims. Home Secretary, Shabana Mahmood, said the government was " rolling out the strongest protections ever available to victims". , external "This government is taking action and will always stand with victims and survivors of domestic abuse," she said. A DAPO can be made by a court to protect victims from all forms of domestic abuse, including non-physical abuse and controlling or coercive behaviour. Applications can also be made by the police, the victim or someone who is not directly involved, known as a third party - such as family member, a friend, or a social worker. Those who breach the order could be charged with a criminal offence, punishable by up to five years in prison. Unlike previous protections, DAPOs can remain in place for as long as necessary in a bid to keep victims safe. title: Substance at Don Toliver Manchester show may be linked to robberies, police say

input.summary: Police are investigating a possible link between the Co-op Live evacuation and reported robberies

More than 12,000 people were evacuated from Manchester's Co-op Live during a performance by US rapper Don Toliver on Sunday. One person was taken to hospital and 88 others were treated at the scene after concertgoers reported a "horrible smell" and some people "coughing up blood". Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said officers received nine reports of jewellery being stolen during the concert but no arrests had been made and the substance had not yet been identified. Image source, PA MEDIA Image caption, The police scene has now been lifted at Co-op Live Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said there was "no wider ongoing risk" to the public. "We are aware similar robberies have been reported at two European concerts for the same artist and will be linking in with our European counterparts to better understand the wider picture of this suspected offending," he said. In a statement on Tuesday evening, Co-op Live said it was conducting a "full review" into the incident. "The safety and security of our guests, artists and staff remain our highest priority, and we take that responsibility extremely seriously." The venue, which opened in 2024, apologised to fans for what should have been an "enjoyable evening" and said it expects no disruption to future events. title: John Stones faces 2028 trial over alleged motoring offence

input.lead: The former Manchester City defender denies failing to provide driver information to police
input.summary: The former Manchester City defender denies failing to provide driver information to police
input.evidence_text: John Stones faces 2028 trial over alleged motoring offence - BBC News Image source, Press Association Image caption, The former Manchester City defender has pleaded not guilty Published 18 minutes ago England defender John Stones faces trial in 2028 over an allegation he failed to provide driver information to police. The 32-year-old footballer, who left Manchester City for Inter Milan this summer , is alleged to have driven his £150,000 Range Rover at 58mph (93km/h) in a 50mph zone on the M60 in March 2026. Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said Stones did not respond to two letters and on 27 April was charged with failing to furnish driver information. He has since pleaded not guilty. Stones is represented by Freeman & Co Solicitors, a law firm whose owner Nick Freeman has advised several celebrity clients in motoring cases and has trademarked his nickname of Mr Loophole. Stones now faces trial on 29 September 2028 at Warrington Magistrates' Court. He has denied receiving the request for information from the police and asked prosecutors to prove it was served. In a letter to the court, Stones's lawyers added: "It was not reasonably practicable for the defendant to give the information within the requisite period." They also claimed GMP included "hearsay" in its single justice procedure notice dated 20 October 2026. Stones's team requested that the trial should last at least two hours and be heard in the morning. They also asked for permission for him to be excused from a pre-trial case management hearing were one to be required. title: Restaurant boss banned over £363k furlough claims

input.lead: The company received £363,040 but failed to provide evidence it was entitled to the money
input.summary: The company received £363,040 but failed to provide evidence it was entitled to the money
input.evidence_text: Restaurant boss banned over £363k furlough claims - BBC News Image source, Google Maps Image caption, The Laundrette opened on Beech Road in Chorlton in 2013 By Haider Saleem North West Published 24 November 2026 The co-founder of a restaurant has been banned from acting as a company director for five years after his company failed to account for over £363,000 in furlough payments during the coronavirus pandemic, the Insolvency Service said. Patrick Hall, 45, helped establish The Laundrette in Chorlton, Manchester, which closed in 2025 after 12 years in business, citing "rising costs and insufficient government support". The Insolvency Service said Winchester Services Limited, which ran the restaurant, repeatedly failed to provide evidence that it was entitled to the payments. Hall, from Levenshulme, agreed to a disqualification undertaking and a five-year ban. The restaurant and bar, known for its pizzas and cocktails, opened on Beech Road in 2013 and was run through several companies under Hall's directorship. Winchester Services Limited received the furlough payments between April 2020 and May 2021. HMRC began examining the claims in July 2022, but the company failed to provide the required information despite being given additional time. In January 2023, HMRC demanded repayment of the full amount and imposed penalties of £344,888 on the company for what it said was a deliberate failure to report the overpayments. When the company went into liquidation in March 2023, it had liabilities of more than £913,000, including nearly £708,000 owed to HMRC over the furlough claims and penalties. title: Memorial plaques and urns worth £20k stolen from Stockport cemetery

input.lead: More than £20,000 worth of memorial plaques and urns were taken from St Mark's Church in Stockport
input.summary: More than £20,000 worth of memorial plaques and urns were taken from St Mark's Church in Stockport
input.evidence_text: Memorial plaques and urns worth £20k stolen from Stockport cemetery - BBC News Image caption, Police said the theft took place between 17:30 on Sunday and 05:30 on Monday By Georgie Docker and Richard Stead , North West Published 24 November 2026 Memorial plaques and grave ornaments worth more than £20,000 have been stolen from a cemetery in Stockport. A volunteer at St Mark's Church in Bredbury discovered about 94 cast-iron memorial plaques and 80 stone and granite flower urns had been stolen at about 05:30 GMT on Monday. Greater Manchester Police said the total estimated value of the stolen items is in excess of £20,000, adding "this figure may increase as further families visit the churchyard and report additional missing items". "You just can't believe it," Reverend Andy Bull said. "For the plaques to have disappeared - the sentimental value of that is huge to people." Image caption, Reverend Andy Bull said it was 'hard to comprehend' that someone would steal memorial plaques and urns Police estimated the memorial plaques were worth more than £8,000 and the stone and granite urns more than £12,000. But Bull said the loss to families was far greater. "People have a very strong affiliation with the graveyard. It's a place where they come to remember loved ones," he said. "A lot of people are feeling very sad that a place which was there to remember loved ones has become fraught with emotions." GMP said it was reviewing CCTV footage to identify any people or vehicles in the area during the period of the theft. By 2030, Transport for Greater Manchester wants 70% of primary school pupils to walk, wheel, scoot or cycle to and from school. Image caption, The School Streets programme is designed to persuade more children to walk to and from school Roads surrounding the Dean Trust Academy are chaotic at peak times, with motorists often parking on double yellow lines or leaving their engines running while waiting for their children to finish school. One parent Lisa Moores said: "It's really busy - loads of children are trying to cross the road at the same time and cars are trying to navigate round them, I've had a few run-ins with people not giving way. "Having restrictions down here would make a big difference during certain times of day." Worthington said he would like to implement the School Streets programme. input.lead: Jamie, 17, has had two emergency operations since falling from a sixth-floor balcony on 10 November
input.summary: Jamie, 17, has had two emergency operations since falling from a sixth-floor balcony on 10 November
input.evidence_text: Benidorm balcony fall: Bury teen Jamie opens eyes after two weeks - BBC News Image source, Family handout Image caption, Jamie, 17, has shown signs of improvement but remains seriously ill in hospital By Haider Saleem North West Published 24 November 2026 A teenager who fell from a sixth-floor hotel balcony in Spain has opened his eyes and responded to his relatives after spending nearly two weeks in intensive care, his family has said. Jamie, 17, was seriously injured in Benidorm on 10 November and has had two emergency operations. His family, from Bury in Greater Manchester, said doctors had been reducing Jamie's sedation and went on to say that he had responded to their voices and had followed instructions. While the teenager's lungs are improving, he remains seriously ill, still requires support from a ventilator and faces further surgery, they said. Image source, Family handout Image caption, Jamie remains seriously ill in hospital in Alicante, Spain, where he has undergone two emergency operations "After so many days of seeing him heavily sedated, we finally got to see those eyes open, see him looking at us, responding to our voices and following instructions," the family said. "After nearly two weeks of worry, waiting and uncertainty, those moments meant more to us than we could ever put into words." Jamie had been on holiday with his mum Gemma and her friends. His aunt Lauren said the family did not know the circumstances which led to him falling from the balcony. Describing how she felt when she learned what had happened, Lauren said it had been "the worst phone call of my life". "Too often, the powerful have been protected and the vulnerable exploited,” he said “We need to get to a place where women and girls feel confident that if they report a crime, they will be treated with dignity and compassion and action will be taken." On Tuesday, the Government said plans to curb the use of NDAs would be brought forward to January The changes under the Employment Rights Act and the Victims and Courts Act will void clauses in NDAs if they are used to silence workers over harassment or discrimination or to stop victims reporting information about criminal conduct

The former Hope United Reformed Church in Chapel Street, Salford , dates from 1819 Close to Manchester city centre and less than 100 yards from Salford Central railway station it ceased to be a regular place of worship several years ago. Grade II listed, it is now up for sale for offers in excess of £1.4m Its roots lie in a surge of "Christian fervour" across the country at the end of the Napoleonic Wars. It sprang from a dearth of places to hear the Gospel in the rapidly industrialising Salford. It survived as a church through name changes, and the resignation of its first leader A dwindling congregation eventually meant a final Sunday Service was held in 2019. In 2023 plans to convert it into a complex of flats, a community centre and commercial use were submitted to the City Council Hope United Reformed Church on Chapel St, Salford, pictured today. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. title: Cherki calls for more following Napoli draw

input.lead: Cherki calls for more following Napoli draw
input.summary: Rasmus Højlund grabbed the opener for the visitors after 55 minutes, latching onto Billy Gilmour’s pass before drilling into the net. Enzo Maresca’s men reacted well to the setback and levelled 12 minutes later thanks to a thunderous left-footed strike from midfield maestro Ayyou
input.evidence_text: Rasmus Højlund grabbed the opener for the visitors after 55 minutes, latching onto Billy Gilmour’s pass before drilling into the net. Enzo Maresca’s men reacted well to the setback and levelled 12 minutes later thanks to a thunderous left-footed strike from midfield maestro Ayyoub Bouaddi, who claimed his first-ever goal in senior football. With City in the ascendancy, the visitors broke on a quick counter and restored their lead through Noa Lang’s controlled volley. But Maresca’s men showed grit and determination to fight back for a second time, with UEFA’s Player of the Match Cherki precisely finding the net with four minutes of normal time left at the Etihad to earn a point. Despite another sparkling individual performance, the Frenchman made it clear that the three points are always the utmost priority. “I don’t care about scoring my goal today. I want to win, just that,” said Cherki in an honest interview after the game. “Today we played good but we didn’t put a lot of energy I think. “We need to do more. We need to win this game, today I don’t care about scoring my goal, we need to win the game. We try to put all we have on the pitch. Sometimes the game is not like how you want. “Today it’s like the last two or three games. We need to work more and come back for a win. Just that.” The draw means we have three wins, one draw and one defeat in the competition this term, with three fixtures left of the League Phase. Attention now turns to Sunday’s huge Premier League clash away to league-leaders Arsenal and Cherki explained that City only have one intention heading into London. “We are in a difficult position, that is true because we didn’t win the game,” he continued. “We’re going to London to win the game. “Nothing more.”
